correctness.rationale: Exact sinc integration handles both \(u\ne0\) and the \(u=0\) axis; separating real and imaginary parts exhausts the zero set. Monotonic \(\tan(v)/v\) and \(v\tan v\) on every tangent branch give a uniform \(2V/\pi+O(1)\) zero census on each exceptional line after excluding removable \(v=\pm p\) roots. Lattice covolume and a bounded-variation semicircle sum yield individual densities. Rational \(\alpha=p/q\) gives overlap exactly at indices divisible by \(q\); on those lines zeros coincide with a \(\pi\)-spaced lattice up to bounded exceptions, giving correction \(2/(\pi q)\). Thus the proof, unlike the numerical diagnostics, covers all radii and every \(0<\alpha<1\).
